title: Why did the 1904 Olympic marathon become infamous?
sources: International Olympic Committee 1904 St. Louis Records
Smithsonian Magazine The 1904 Olympic Marathon Mayhem

lines.text: The nineteen-oh-four Olympic marathon in St. Louis was so wildly disastrous, it felt like a slapstick comedy film.
Runners raced twenty-five miles through ninety-degree heat over dusty unpaved roads choked with car exhaust.
lines.caps: Runners choked on *dust clouds | in 90-degree summer *heat

lines.text: The race organizers intentionally provided only one single water station to test human dehydration limits.
lines.caps: Organizers provided only *one | water station for the entire *race!

lines.text: One runner hitched a ride in an automobile for eleven miles, crossed the finish line, and almost took the gold medal.
lines.caps: One runner rode in a *car | for 11 miles and nearly won *gold!

lines.text: Another runner ate rotten apples from an orchard, developed agonizing stomach cramps, and took an hour nap by the road.
lines.caps: Another took a *nap | by the road after eating rotten *apples

lines.text: The actual winner was repeatedly injected with rat poison strychnine and raw egg whites as a stimulant, hallucinating across the finish line.
lines.caps: The winner was *dosed with rat poison | as a performance *drug!

lines.text: It remains the most bizarre and chaotic athletic event ever staged in Olympic history.
lines.caps: The most chaotic athletic *event | ever staged on *Earth!
